title: Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)
shortDefinition: A family of techniques for adapting large pre-trained models by training only a small subset of parameters, dramatically reducing compute requirements.
definition: Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) is a family of techniques for adapting large pre-trained models to specific tasks by training only a small subset of parameters — or adding a small number of new parameters — rather than updating all of the original model's billions of parameters, dramatically reducing the compute and memory requirements of fine-tuning while achieving similar adaptation quality. PEFT has made fine-tuning large language models practically accessible for organizations that can't afford full fine-tuning's substantial compute requirements.

sections.title: LoRA: The most widely used PEFT technique
sections.description: LoRA adds small adapter matrices of lower rank, training only these while keeping original model weights frozen.

content.text: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is currently the most widely adopted PEFT approach — it adds small 'adapter' matrices of much lower rank than the original model's weight matrices, training only these adapters while keeping the original model weights frozen. This allows the model to learn task-specific adaptations through these compact adapters, requiring far fewer trainable parameters (typically 0.1–1% of the full model's parameters) than full fine-tuning, with adaptation quality competitive with full fine-tuning for many tasks. QLoRA extends this further by additionally quantizing the base model weights during training, enabling LoRA fine-tuning of very large models on significantly less GPU memory.

items: LoRA — adds low-rank adapter matrices, freezes original weights.
Trainable parameters — typically 0.1–1% of full model size.
Adaptation quality — competitive with full fine-tuning for many tasks.
QLoRA — adds quantization for even lower memory requirements.
Memory efficiency — enables fine-tuning of very large models on less GPU memory.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: LoRA fine-tunes only 0.1–1% of model parameters — achieving competitive quality with a fraction of the compute.

sections.title: Why PEFT changed the economics of LLM fine-tuning

content.text: Before PEFT techniques like LoRA, fine-tuning a large language model required updating all its parameters with each training step — computationally and memory-intensive, requiring expensive GPU infrastructure for models at the scale of today's leading LLMs. PEFT techniques made fine-tuning computationally feasible for organizations without access to massive training clusters, since training only small adapter matrices requires a fraction of the GPU memory and compute of full fine-tuning. This shifted fine-tuning from a prohibitively expensive operation for most organizations to an accessible customization approach.

Accessibility — made fine-tuning practical for most organizations.
Economic shift — from prohibitively expensive to accessible.

items: "Does LoRA/PEFT actually produce models as good as full fine-tuning?" — For many task-specific fine-tuning applications, LoRA achieves performance close to full fine-tuning with dramatically less compute — ClickMasters validates this directly for your specific task rather than assuming either parity or meaningful gap.
"How much will this cost?" — $15,000–$75,000 depending on model size, task complexity, and whether multi-task adapter composition is needed. Fixed quote after Discovery.

"Should we use PEFT or full fine-tuning for our specific use case?" — This depends on model size, available compute, and adaptation depth required — ClickMasters recommends the right approach during Discovery, sometimes including an explicit comparison when the choice isn't clear from task characteristics alone.

"Can PEFT adapters be removed or swapped after training?" — Yes, this is one of LoRA's practical advantages — adapters can be added to or removed from the base model, enabling efficient deployment of multiple task-specific fine-tuned variants.

content.text: PEFT has limitations. It may not match full fine-tuning performance for tasks requiring deep behavioral adaptation or significant capability changes. The quality gap between PEFT and full fine-tuning varies by task and model size. QLoRA quantization can introduce accuracy tradeoffs. PEFT techniques are primarily applicable to open-source models, not proprietary provider APIs. The adapter approach adds complexity to deployment and versioning. PEFT may not be appropriate for tasks where the full model's behavior needs to change fundamentally.

items.question: What's the difference between LoRA and QLoRA?
items.answer: LoRA trains small adapter matrices while keeping original weights in standard precision; QLoRA also quantizes the base model weights during training, enabling fine-tuning of larger models on less GPU memory.

items.question: Can PEFT adapters be removed or swapped after training?
items.answer: Yes, this is one of LoRA's practical advantages — adapters can be added to or removed from the base model, enabling efficient deployment of multiple task-specific fine-tuned variants without maintaining entirely separate model copies for each task.

items.question: Does PEFT work for proprietary models like GPT-4, or only open-source models?
items.answer: Provider fine-tuning APIs for models like GPT-3.5 use their own fine-tuning infrastructure; PEFT techniques like LoRA are primarily applied to open-source models you deploy yourself.

items.question: How much less compute does LoRA need compared to full fine-tuning?
items.answer: This varies by model size and rank settings, but LoRA typically trains 0.1–1% of full model parameters, with proportionate compute reduction compared to updating all parameters.

items.question: How long does a PEFT fine-tuning project take?
items.answer: 4–18 weeks depending on model size, task complexity, and validation requirements.

items.question: Can multiple LoRA adapters be combined for different tasks?
items.answer: Yes, adapter composition is an active research and practical application area — ClickMasters evaluates this where serving multiple task-specific fine-tuned variants efficiently is a requirement.

items.question: What is the rank in LoRA and how does it affect performance?
items.answer: The rank determines the size of the adapter matrices. Higher rank adapters can capture more complex adaptations but require more compute. ClickMasters tunes rank settings for your specific task to balance performance and efficiency.

items.question: What is the difference between LoRA and adapters?
items.answer: Adapters add small trainable layers to the model. LoRA is a specific type of adapter-based approach that uses low-rank matrices. LoRA is currently the most widely used adapter technique due to its efficiency and performance.

items.question: Can PEFT be used for computer vision models?
items.answer: Yes — PEFT techniques like LoRA can be applied to vision models and vision-language models, not just language models. The same efficiency benefits apply to vision fine-tuning tasks.

items.question: What is the relationship between PEFT and model distillation?
items.answer: PEFT makes fine-tuning more efficient. Distillation creates smaller models from larger ones. Both improve efficiency — PEFT for adaptation, distillation for inference. They can be combined for maximum efficiency.
